ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $O$ is a point on line $AB$, with $CO \perp DO$, and $OE$ bisects $\angle BOC$. If $\angle COE = \frac{1}{3}\angle DOB$, determine the measure of $\angle AOC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle COE=x^\circ$, then $\angle DOB=3x^\circ$ \\
$\because OE$ bisects $\angle BOC$ \\
$\therefore \angle BOE=\angle COE=x^\circ$ \\
$\because CO\perp DO$ \\
$\therefore \angle DOC=90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore x^\circ+x^\circ+3x^\circ=90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore x=18$ \\
$\therefore \angle BOE=\angle COE=18^\circ$ \\
$\therefore \angle AOC=\angle AOB-\angle BOE-\angle COE=180^\circ-18^\circ-18^\circ=\boxed{144^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle COE=x^\circ$, then $\angle DOB=3x^\circ$ \\ $\because OE$ bisects $\angle BOC$ \\ $\therefore \angle BOE=\angle COE=x^\circ$ \\ $\because CO\perp DO$ \\ $\therefore \angle DOC=90^\circ$ \\ $\therefore x^\circ+x^\circ+3x^\circ=90^\circ$ \\ $\therefore x=18$ \\ $\therefore \angle BOE=\angle COE=18^\circ$ \\ $\therefore \angle AOC=\angle AOB-\angle BOE-\angle COE=180^\circ-18^\circ-18^\circ=\boxed{144^\circ}$

Image description: In the figure, A, O, and B are on the same horizontal straight line, A is to the left of O, and B is to the right of O; from O there are also three rays, OC goes to the upper right, OE is located between OC and OB, OD goes to the lower right, and OB is located between OE and OD.
Reasoning: From the problem statement, CO ⟂ DO, so ∠COD = 90°. Because OE bisects ∠BOC, let ∠COE = x°, then ∠EOB = x°. Also because ∠COE = 1/3 ∠DOB, so ∠DOB = 3x°. According to the order of the rays in the figure, ∠COD is composed of three parts, ∠COE, ∠EOB, and ∠BOD, therefore x + x + 3x = 90, giving 5x = 90, x = 18. Thus ∠BOC = ∠BOE + ∠EOC = 18° + 18° = 36°. Since A, O, and B are collinear, ∠AOB = 180°, so ∠AOC = 180° - 36° = 144°.
